problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a critical inspection circuit for twelve regional warehouses, each situated at distinct geographical points.  
Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (101,39)  
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at grid reference (45,130)  
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (19,34)  
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at grid reference (195,52)  
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (200,198)  
Warehouse Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (127,145)  
Warehouse Eta: Positioned at grid reference (196,178)  
Warehouse Theta: Positioned at grid reference (54,60)  
Warehouse Iota: Positioned at grid reference (187,33)  
Warehouse Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (59,194)  
Warehouse Lambda: Positioned at grid reference (98,90)  
Warehouse Mu: Positioned at grid reference (155,151)

Eta to Theta: 184.6 km

Due to a permanent infrastructure restriction, no direct transport link exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.  
Furthermore, owing to regulatory scheduling constraints, exactly one of the following two connections must be incorporated into the inspection loop: the route linking Beta and Gamma, or the route linking Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal‑distance closed circuit that visits every warehouse exactly once and concludes at the origin point.
